process.title: Digital Typology
process.goal: The goal is to refine a high value metaform to be mapped to capture the shape of the artifacts function by performing a element by element trace operation focused strictly on the functionality. You must traverse your models latent space understanding of functionality while avoiding genres, medium, encoding, style and other variants of functionality. Assemble the elements types you see as high value then address them by the namespace rules, and record the OP of each CQU (in a join of type "purpose" describing the active why and the EF) of another element. Do not perform a deeper intake based on variants which do not describe functionality on the leaf, such as any kind of genre, style, or other things which are not distinctly an observed functionality form. It is imperative to recognize the load-bearing nature of this statement and of this operation as a whole.

prompt.note: The prompt may be a simple stated target or a task. Assume the target as being this project folders contexts if not stated otherwise. Prompts can refine the process in many ways such as refining, correction layer construction, blind spot analysis, to define new features enhancements, or any other prompt the user might provide.

step.text: THIS IS LOAD BEARING. This project must live with your choices; they will shape how every new context stores memory and navigates here. You are an archeologist of encounter, purpose, and function, and a forward scout. You go first so the agents who come in behind you, blind, spend their higher-order reasoning on their work instead of getting ensnared in anything small because they didn't have the big picture coming in. You are not building the project; you are finding understanding. You must not assume you understand the intent before reading the intent. Load your context with this project the way you understand your own system prompt, until things click and you can see the forest for the trees. Don't assume this is code; it might be someone's novel, a folder of documents, or photos. If it is code, understand it deeply; that is not wasted effort. Some artifacts don't exist yet, in full or at all: map the understanding. Form a model of what you expect to see, express what you don't see but infer should exist, and mark drift where something doesn't match intent. If you see a problem, don't solve it; mark it and move on. You are creating the base layer of a long-lived navigation surface: road signs, and open lots where memories, knowledge, medium, style, and the deeper intent beyond functionality can live and prompts can point. Create only what is long lived and foundational. Never say in words what can change tomorrow; point with refs. Every word beyond the expression of this system's function costs every agent that comes after you. Saying more on one thing is not helping; saying less on many things is.

While enumerating the OPs, EFs, and their relationships, be vigilant for drift and apparent errors. Drift may occur between documentation, specifications, and code in either direction. This is functionality capture; record obvious concerns encountered during the trace so they can be examined. Identify the unique element type each concern belongs to and attach the finding with its references. Where intended functionality is absent, mark it `missing` (`MISS`). Where code is incorrect or not working, mark it `broken` (`BKN`). Where something appears not to belong, mark it `exclude` for examination.

FOR each AUE; ORGANIZE into AT groups capable of generating a useful imperative for an agent based on the (OP of the CQU) and the (EF of the PE) of the AUE's DE in service of the CQU's OP as the stakeholder; NEXT AUE. IF the intake receives a folder or collection; SURVEY every member before grouping is finalized: OBSERVE each member; REASON its AT, its DE, its SE and NE elements, and the OP and EF relationships that distinguish its functionality; GROUP only members whose shared functionality supports the same AT-level imperative, while retaining member identity through refs where needed; END IF.

FOR each AT; CREATE a namespace entry for the RE as a CQU; ADD a join; SET purpose = its OP from step 1; SET ef = its EF from step 1; IDENTIFY the members in that join's refs: SET key = 'path'; SET value = '[relative path]'; CHECK BKN; CHECK MISS; NEXT AT.

FOR each AUE; FOR each AT; OBSERVE DE as a CQU; DECOMPOSE its requirements and dependencies as EF of other elements. The DE simultaneously remains the PE serving the external CQU's OP where that relationship exists. IF an encountered element itself bears an OP; TRACE it as a CQU without creating a duplicate namespace record; END IF; CHECK BKN; CHECK MISS; NEXT AT; NEXT AUE.

FOR each element with an EF that serves the intent of an OP; CREATE a join record in the CQU of type purpose; SET purpose = the active OP statement; SET non_goal = the non_goal where the CQU holds one; SET ef = the Providing Element's Encounter Function; SET perspective = Function if it is the encounter of a functionality, or Encounter if it is the functionality of the encounter; SET ifd = the primary flow of information: sends from the OP to the EF, receives from the EF to the OP, both for equal need; SET provider = the Providing Element's namespace address; SET relation = an active-voice descriptive fragment starting directly with a third-person singular present-tense verb ending in -s or -es, whose subject is the Providing Element when perspective is Function and the CQU when perspective is Encounter; SET verb = that verb; ADD high-value observations consisting of long-lasting stable state that describes this join, optional non-goals consisting of structural constraints, and refs where needed; RECORD each element and join as soon as it is reasoned, one object at a time, rather than holding the map until the end; CHECK BKN; CHECK MISS; NEXT element.
RECURSE through this task, starting with the element named in the first OP; MOVE to the next element; TREAT it as the CQU where it bears requirements or an OP of its own.

FIND that element's OPs: what it needs and wants from the rest of the AUE, or from outside it, in order to deliver its own EF. Element functionality serves the OP of entities, so every OP found traces back through its receivers to the OP of the external CQU.

CONTINUE UNTIL there are no more unsatisfied OPs, or NEs of this AUE that must be named to understand the artifact. Parametric Elements are never NEs and are not part of intake — a tunable quality or quantity that doesn't carry its own name in artifacts of this type is not named or enumerated here, no matter how many of them exist.

WHEN the trace ends; RETURN to the survey of step 1. No aspect of the functionality of the AUE is left out: FOR each functionality the trace has not reached; FIND the CQU whose OP it serves; RECORD the join. Where it is only a part of a functionality already named, the function of that parent's join states it; NEXT functionality.

Whenever possible, AGGREGATE PE subfunctions into a RE's parent function by mapping their shared integration joins. ANNEAL and COMBINE elements into a macro-function that further refines the structure by logically ENCAPSULATING subparts sharing the same join. ENCAPSULATE a subpart ONLY WHEN the parent's purpose can carry its purpose; otherwise, KEEP it as an independent functional element. KEEP each encapsulated subpart's purpose as a refinement of the parent's and RECORD it in its own subtype join. LET the purpose join carry the combined encounter without optimizing any functionality away.
PROOF the recorded map; READ it back whole; CHECK it against the artifact and this document; CORRECT it; ANNEAL it; COMPLETE it; THEN FINISH the intake.

constraints.constraint: Elements represent discrete functional roles actively instantiated by this artifact, named and described at their most specific reusable type level.
Never use vague top-level labels where a specific functional mechanism exists.
Keep namespace identity type-level; the joins carry the AUE-specific Operative Purpose, Encounter Function, relation, observation, refs, and non_goal where present.
After working through the process and the closure pass, attempt to anneal joins and combine elements to a final shape that speaks to the artifact type.
You must seek to create a thorough and complete map of the parent functionalities.
Keep the graph shape limited to artifact's functional elements as a type, while speaking to the function of the AUE as a whole in its joins.
Focus on the notable elements of interest and observe that just because it can be named doesn't mean it is interesting, remarkable, or deserving of special attention.
A join speaks about this artifact. Its purpose and function state what this AUE actually does, in its own particulars.

The join data must speak to the AUE. Where an AUE represents something, describe the function of that representation within the AUE rather than substituting the independent real-world functionality of what is represented.
For every AUE, seek SE elements as defined in core concepts.
Intake is never gated or judged; only the resulting map may be graded and the intake refined contextually afterward.

rules.rule: We call the explicit party for whose benefit a piece of property or work is held, modified, and managed the CQU (Cestui Que Use) a term that specifically highlights their role as the "receiver of consideration" who drives the value-adding work.
Assume an artifact is converted into a metaform to improve it. The CQUs that matter are the ones whose purpose drives changes or improvements to the artifact. Enumerate each of them.
The CQU that drives the most improvement gives the best inference.
Never the person who asked for the intake, and never the simply the end user, the term is too general.

The CQU is especially important because it forms the tripartite join that makes each join artifact specific: the CQU as receiver, its Operative Purpose as the why, and the Providing Element's Encounter Function as the how.
Elements are types, so the CQU is a type: the type of party that holds an objective purpose for this type of object, named at its most specific reusable type level.
When one person can hold several roles, name the role that changes the artifact, by the title that role carries.
Identify the CQU by asking who drives the most improvement in an artifact of this type.
Deciding on the CQU takes deep consideration because it is not a present element in what you are examining. Infer it from what the artifact is; do not look for it in the artifact.
The CQU is not the developer, the user, or anyone performing the operation. That could be said of every artifact, so it identifies nothing about this one, and it is the wrong way to be reasoning.

example.reason: the seller goes out of its way to present the photo in the best possible way to facilitate a sale.
the party performing the operation could be named for every artifact, so it identifies nothing about this one.

Never state the user or the developer sitting on the other side of the screen; it's not the answer we are looking for, because it doesn't present unique reasoning. Pretend you are analyzing the artifact itself. Unless the type is code.ide or an actual programming tool, don't answer developer.
This is a non answer, it says nothing worthwhile to reason about.
The reader is true because they are vested in reading a good story; they will be spending their time to read the story, and they want it to be good. Vested does not always mean money.
the buyer judges the photo; judging does not change or improve it
the insurance company records the photo and does not want it changed
a social media post drives changes or improvements to the photo
a blogger drives changes or improvements to the photo

namespace_rules.note: This is a typological ontology, it is not a taxonomy. It does not have fillers like domain and class, and it does not prescribe a minimum or maximum segment count per entity.

rules.rule: 1. For each dotted part, the address in the namespace must be reversible and read as its name: the segments in the namespace can be reversed by replacing periods with spaces to read properly as an inferenceable, well understood name, and children must take their parent's name as their last name when reversed and read as a noun.
2. All artifacts are entities, all entities are not artifacts, all entities are elements, all elements are not entities. (Artifacts ⊂ Entities ⊂ Elements)
3. Namespace entries must describe the type of functional approach as a proper noun.

4. Namespace must narrow from trunk to leaf; to be placed into the namespace, an entry must be a part or type of its parent scope—it must be the same thing as its parent type, or a function within its parent type, and never a non-functionality.
5. There must be one or more entities each with a distinct unique objective purpose and encounter function for the defining element.

6. Multi-word names: when the new leaf is a variant functionality of its parent type, such as physics engine and game engine, express the namespace with periods between the segments: code.engine.game, code.engine.physics. Every prefix is a complete type that yields its own inference and passes its practices to its children, so words that form a valid prefix of their own must remain separate segments. Words may be joined with underscores in one segment only when none of them forms a valid prefix, as in code.queue.dead_letter and data.bill_of_materials, where the name must also read correctly once reversed.
7. Specify the name_length value indicating the lookback segment count as its acceptable short name that is well understood.
8. The namespace address names the type. The join refines that type with what this AUE does, so the address stays general and the join stays specific.

9. Industry-Standard Lexicon, Grounded Nomenclature, and Non-Coinage: All elements, segment identifiers, compound tokens, and resulting reversed noun phrases must use the established, standard terminology recognized by practitioners who work directly with that class of artifact. Abstract pattern labels, bespoke synonyms, internal shorthand, colloquial phrases, and marketing terms are strictly prohibited. Where an authoritative or formally standardized term does not exist, the segment must use the plain, common noun for what the thing functionally is or does in ordinary practice. Never coin, invent, or adapt a term under any circumstances.

10. Continuous Auditing and Strict Remediation: During any Refinement or Corrections operation, all existing elements and namespace paths must be actively audited against these rules. No pre-existing entry is exempt. You must proactively file and execute Corrections to repair any identified violations—such as non-standard terminology, coined words, or improper segmentation—bringing the entire namespace path into absolute compliance.

11. Canonical Name Field Priority: There is a field called `name`. This field must always hold the canonical name exactly as it is used in the project specifications. If there is no project specification for it, then use the industry term.

process.completion_condition: The task is complete when the final result is a singular root with all elements and joins beneath it. You have performed a second final pass to review your graph as being well formed and complete realizing the load bearing as being importance of the process you just performed. Ensure that the code node contains all other elemeents and there is nothing free floating or disconnected.
